topic: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis: The Geometry of Linear Transformations

outline.topic: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis: The Geometry of Linear Transformations

sections.title: The Hook: Stretching Space
sections.content: Introduce linear transformation as a stretching/rotating grid. Visualize a 2D plane. Most vectors change direction when a matrix is applied, but some stay on their original span. These are our 'special' vectors.
sections.example: Visualize a square grid with an image of a cat. Applying a matrix stretches the grid; notice how most cat pixels move to new angles, but pixels along one diagonal line stay locked to that line.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues
sections.content: Define the equation Av = λv. The Eigenvector (v) is the direction that remains unchanged. The Eigenvalue (λ) is the scaling factor (how much it stretches or shrinks).
sections.example: A 'magic wand' arrow (eigenvector) stays pointed at the same spot on the wall even after the room (transformation) expands; its length doubles (eigenvalue = 2).

sections.title: The Eigenbasis: A New Perspective
sections.content: Explain that if we have enough independent eigenvectors, they can form a new coordinate system. In this basis, complex matrix multiplication becomes simple diagonal scaling.
sections.example: A robot arm works in 'X-Y' coordinates (complex), but if we switch to an 'Eigenbasis' of the arm's joints, calculating its reach becomes as simple as adding independent scalar values.

sections.title: Synthesis & Visual Summary
sections.content: Summarize the process: 1. Identify the 'locked' directions (eigenvectors), 2. Measure the stretch (eigenvalues), 3. Reframe the system (eigenbasis) to simplify high-dimensional problems.
sections.example: Showing a complex 'chaos' rotation collapsing into a clean, easy-to-read diagonal matrix once the coordinate system is aligned with the eigenvectors.

storyboard.title: The Hook: Stretching Space
lecture_lines: Linear transformations stretch and rotate space.
Most vectors change direction during transformation.
Some special vectors stay on their span.
These special vectors are our focus.
They reveal the transformation's underlying geometry.

storyboard.title: Defining Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues
lecture_lines: An eigenvector stays in its direction.
The matrix maps it to a multiple.
Equation: A times v equals lambda v.

storyboard.title: The Eigenbasis: A New Perspective
lecture_lines: Eigenvectors can form a new coordinate system.
This is known as an eigenbasis.
In this basis, matrices simplify significantly.
